summary: The Governance pillar of the World Economic Forum's Stakeholder Capitalism Metrics: how the company's purpose, governing body, stakeholder engagement, ethical behaviour and risk and opportunity oversight are run. It has 6 core and 6 expanded metrics.

questions.text: Does your company have a formally stated purpose?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: The British Academy and Colin Mayer, GRI (102-26), EPIC, and others. Answer yes if the purpose is written down and approved by the company, not just informal.

questions.text: What is your company's stated purpose, in the company's own words?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: The British Academy and Colin Mayer, GRI (102-26), EPIC, and others. Quote or summarise the purpose statement. It should express how the business proposes solutions to economic, environmental and social issues.

questions.text: Does your stated purpose describe how the company solves economic, environmental or social problems?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: The British Academy and Colin Mayer, GRI (102-26), EPIC, and others. Purpose is the expression of the means by which a business proposes solutions to economic, environmental and social issues.

questions.text: Which stakeholder groups does your stated purpose say the company creates value for?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: The British Academy and Colin Mayer, GRI (102-26), EPIC, and others. Corporate purpose should create value for all stakeholders, including shareholders. Select every group named in the purpose.

questions.text: Who approved the company's stated purpose?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: The British Academy and Colin Mayer, GRI (102-26), EPIC, and others. Choose the highest body or person that formally approved the purpose statement.

questions.text: Where is your stated purpose publicly available?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: The British Academy and Colin Mayer, GRI (102-26), EPIC, and others. Give the document or web page, for example the annual report or website.

disclosures.title: Quality of governing body: Governance body composition

questions.text: How many members does your highest governance body have in total?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count all current members of the highest governance body (for example the board). Report a whole number.

questions.text: What are the names of the committees of your highest governance body?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). List each committee, for example audit, remuneration, nomination, sustainability. Composition questions apply to the body and each committee.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body have competencies relating to economic topics?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count members with experience or expertise in economic topics such as finance, strategy or markets.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body have competencies relating to environmental topics?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count members with experience or expertise in environmental topics such as climate, resources or biodiversity.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body have competencies relating to social topics?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count members with experience or expertise in social topics such as labour, human rights, health and safety or community.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body are executive members?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Executive members are also employed in management roles of the company. Report a whole number.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body are non-executive members?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Non-executive members do not hold management roles in the company. Report a whole number.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body are independent?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count members who meet your or your regulator's independence criteria. State the criteria used in your notes if possible.

questions.text: What is the average tenure, in years, of members on the highest governance body?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Average number of years members have served on the governance body. Also note the longest tenure if available.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body hold other significant positions or commitments?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count members with significant positions elsewhere, such as other boards or major organisations.

questions.text: What is the nature of the other significant positions and commitments held by governance body members?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Describe the nature of the commitments, for example other company boards, public office or non-profit roles, and the number held by each member.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body are women?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Report the number by gender. Also report any members of another gender identity, if applicable.

questions.text: How many members of the highest governance body belong to under-represented social groups?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Count members from groups under-represented in your context, such as minority or indigenous groups, or people with disabilities, where you can lawfully collect this.

questions.text: How are stakeholders represented on the highest governance body?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-22), GRI (405-1a), IR (4B). Describe how stakeholders such as employees, shareholders or communities have representation, for example elected employee representatives.

disclosures.title: Stakeholder engagement: Material issues impacting stakeholders

questions.text: Who are your key stakeholder groups?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). List the groups your company has identified as key stakeholders, for example employees, customers, suppliers, communities, investors.

questions.text: Which topics are material to your key stakeholders?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). Provide the list of topics that matter most to your stakeholders.

questions.text: Which topics are material to the company itself?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). Provide the list of topics that matter most to the company's success and impacts.

questions.text: How were the material topics identified?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). Describe the process, such as materiality assessment, surveys, interviews or benchmarking.

questions.text: How were stakeholders engaged in identifying the material topics?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). Describe the methods used, such as surveys, interviews, workshops or consultations, and how often.

questions.text: Which methods did you use to engage stakeholders?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). Select all that apply.

questions.text: When was your list of material topics last reviewed or updated?
questions.hint: Stakeholder engagement · Source: GRI (102-21), GRI (102-43), GRI (102-47). Give the month and year of the latest review.

questions.text: Does your company have anti-corruption policies and procedures?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Answer yes if written policies and procedures exist.

questions.text: What percentage of governance body members received training on your anti-corruption policies and procedures?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Governance body members trained divided by total members, times 100.

questions.text: What percentage of employees received training on your anti-corruption policies and procedures?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Employees trained divided by total employees, times 100.

questions.text: What percentage of business partners received training on your anti-corruption policies and procedures?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Business partners trained divided by total business partners, times 100.

questions.text: How does anti-corruption training coverage differ by region?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). For each region, give the percentage of governance body members, employees and business partners trained.

questions.text: How many incidents of corruption were confirmed during this year but related to previous years?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Count only incidents confirmed in the current reporting year that occurred in earlier years.

questions.text: What was the nature of the corruption incidents confirmed this year that related to previous years?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Describe the type, for example bribery, facilitation payments, kickbacks or fraud.

questions.text: How many incidents of corruption were confirmed this year and related to this year?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Count incidents both occurring and confirmed in the current reporting year.

questions.text: What was the nature of the corruption incidents confirmed this year that related to this year?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Describe the type, for example bribery, facilitation payments, kickbacks or fraud.

questions.text: What initiatives do you have to improve the broader operating environment and culture to combat corruption?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Describe initiatives such as collective action, industry codes or support for anti-corruption programmes.

questions.text: What stakeholder engagement do you do to combat corruption?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (205-2) and GRI (205-3). Describe how you work with stakeholders such as suppliers, peers, governments and civil society on anti-corruption.

disclosures.title: Ethical behaviour: Protected ethics advice and reporting mechanisms

questions.text: Does your company have an internal mechanism for seeking advice about ethical and lawful behaviour?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). For example an ethics helpline, ethics officer or compliance contact.

questions.text: What internal mechanisms can people use to seek advice about ethical and lawful behaviour and organizational integrity?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). Describe each mechanism and who can use it.

questions.text: Does your company have an external mechanism for seeking advice about ethical and lawful behaviour?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). For example an independent third-party advice line.

questions.text: What external mechanisms can people use to seek advice about ethical and lawful behaviour and organizational integrity?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). Describe each mechanism and who can use it.

questions.text: Does your company have an internal mechanism for reporting concerns about unethical or unlawful behaviour?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). For example a whistleblowing line or reporting to a manager or compliance function.

questions.text: What internal mechanisms can people use to report concerns about unethical or unlawful behaviour and lack of organizational integrity?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). Describe each mechanism and who can use it.

questions.text: Does your company have an external mechanism for reporting concerns about unethical or unlawful behaviour?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). For example an independent hotline run by a third party.

questions.text: What external mechanisms can people use to report concerns about unethical or unlawful behaviour and lack of organizational integrity?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). Describe each mechanism and who can use it.

questions.text: Can concerns be reported anonymously?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). Answer yes if people can report without giving their identity.

questions.text: Are people who report concerns protected from retaliation?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). The metric refers to protected mechanisms. Describe the protection in your notes if possible.

questions.text: Who can use your advice and reporting mechanisms?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI (102-17). Select all that apply.

disclosures.title: Risk and opportunity oversight: Integrating risk and opportunity into business process

questions.text: Does your company publicly disclose its risk factors and opportunities?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). For example in an annual report or other public filing.

questions.text: What are the principal material risks facing your company specifically?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). List risks specific to your company, not generic sector risks.

questions.text: What are the principal material opportunities facing your company specifically?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). List opportunities specific to your company, not generic sector opportunities.

questions.text: What is your company's appetite in respect of these risks?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Describe how much risk the company is willing to accept for each principal risk.

questions.text: How have these risks and opportunities moved over time?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Describe whether each has grown, shrunk or changed compared with earlier periods.

questions.text: How did your company respond to these changes in risks and opportunities?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Describe the actions taken.

questions.text: Do your risk and opportunity disclosures include material economic issues?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Answer yes if economic issues are integrated into the risk and opportunity process.

questions.text: Do your risk and opportunity disclosures include material environmental issues?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Answer yes if environmental issues are integrated into the risk and opportunity process.

questions.text: Do your risk and opportunity disclosures include material social issues?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Answer yes if social issues are integrated into the risk and opportunity process.

questions.text: Do your risk and opportunity disclosures include climate change?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Answer yes if climate-related risks and opportunities are covered.

questions.text: Do your risk and opportunity disclosures include data stewardship?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: EPIC, GRI (102-15), WEF Integrated Corporate Governance, IR (4D). Answer yes if risks and opportunities relating to data protection, privacy and ethical use of data are covered.

questions.text: Is your stated purpose reflected in your company strategy?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: GRI (102-26). Answer yes if the strategy explicitly refers to or is built from the purpose.

questions.text: How is your stated purpose embedded in your company strategies?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: GRI (102-26). Give examples of how strategic decisions reflect the purpose.

questions.text: Is your stated purpose reflected in your company policies?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: GRI (102-26). Answer yes if policies refer to or are aligned with the purpose.

questions.text: How is your stated purpose embedded in your company policies?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: GRI (102-26). Give examples of policies shaped by the purpose.

questions.text: Is your stated purpose reflected in your company goals?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: GRI (102-26). Answer yes if company goals or targets are linked to the purpose.

questions.text: How is your stated purpose embedded in your company goals?
questions.hint: Governing purpose · Source: GRI (102-26). Give examples of goals or targets linked to the purpose.

disclosures.title: Quality of governing body: Progress against strategic milestones

questions.text: Which material economic strategic milestones do you expect to achieve in the following year?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. List the material economic milestones expected next year.

questions.text: Which material environmental strategic milestones do you expect to achieve in the following year?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. List the material environmental milestones expected next year.

questions.text: Which material social strategic milestones do you expect to achieve in the following year?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. List the material social milestones expected next year.

questions.text: Which material strategic milestones from the previous year did you achieve?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. List the economic, environmental and social milestones achieved.

questions.text: What percentage of last year's planned strategic milestones did you achieve?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. Milestones achieved divided by milestones planned, times 100.

questions.text: How are the expected milestones expected to contribute to long-term value?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. Explain the link between next year's milestones and long-term value.

questions.text: How have the milestones achieved in the previous year contributed to long-term value?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: EPIC. Explain the actual contribution to long-term value.

questions.text: Do the performance criteria in the remuneration policies relate to economic objectives of the highest governance body and senior executives?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Answer yes if pay is linked to economic objectives connected to purpose, strategy and long-term value.

questions.text: Do the performance criteria in the remuneration policies relate to environmental objectives of the highest governance body and senior executives?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Answer yes if pay is linked to environmental objectives connected to purpose, strategy and long-term value.

questions.text: Do the performance criteria in the remuneration policies relate to social objectives of the highest governance body and senior executives?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Answer yes if pay is linked to social objectives connected to purpose, strategy and long-term value.

questions.text: How do the performance criteria connect to your stated purpose, strategy and long-term value?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Describe the link between remuneration criteria and purpose, strategy and long-term value.

questions.text: What are your policies on fixed pay and variable pay for the highest governance body and senior executives?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Include performance-based pay, equity-based pay, bonuses, and deferred or vested shares.

questions.text: What is your policy on sign-on bonuses or recruitment incentive payments?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Describe the policy for the highest governance body and senior executives.

questions.text: What is your policy on termination payments?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Describe the policy for the highest governance body and senior executives.

questions.text: Do you have clawback provisions in remuneration policies?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Clawbacks allow the company to recover pay already given, for example after misconduct or restatements.

questions.text: What are your clawback policies?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Describe when and how pay can be recovered.

questions.text: What are your retirement benefit policies for the highest governance body and senior executives?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Describe the benefit schemes and contribution rates.

questions.text: How do retirement benefit schemes and contribution rates for the highest governance body and senior executives differ from those of all other employees?
questions.hint: Quality of governing body · Source: GRI (102-35). Describe differences in schemes and contribution rates.

disclosures.title: Ethical behaviour: Alignment of strategy and policies to lobbying

questions.text: Does your company participate in public policy development or lobbying?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI 415: Public Policy 2016. Include direct lobbying and lobbying through associations.

questions.text: Which significant issues are the focus of your participation in public policy development and lobbying?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI 415: Public Policy 2016. List the main areas of focus.

questions.text: What is your company's strategy relevant to these areas of focus?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI 415: Public Policy 2016. Describe the company strategy for each lobbying focus area.

questions.text: Do your lobbying positions differ from your stated purpose, policies, goals or other public positions?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI 415: Public Policy 2016. Answer yes if any lobbying position differs from what you say publicly.

questions.text: What are the differences between your lobbying positions and your stated purpose, policies, goals or other public positions?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: GRI 415: Public Policy 2016. Describe each difference and the reason for it.

disclosures.title: Ethical behaviour: Monetary losses from unethical behaviour

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with fraud?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Report in your reporting currency for the reporting year.

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with insider trading?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Report in your reporting currency for the reporting year.

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with anti-trust or anti-competitive behaviour?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Report in your reporting currency for the reporting year.

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with market manipulation?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Report in your reporting currency for the reporting year.

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with malpractice?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Report in your reporting currency for the reporting year.

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from legal proceedings associated with violations of other related industry laws or regulations?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Report in your reporting currency for the reporting year.

questions.text: What was the total amount of monetary losses from all of these legal proceedings?
questions.hint: Ethical behaviour · Source: SASB (510a.1). Sum of fraud, insider trading, anti-trust, anti-competitive behaviour, market manipulation, malpractice and other related violations. Include fines, settlements and legal costs.

disclosures.title: Risk and opportunity oversight: Economic, environmental, and social topics in capital allocation framework

questions.text: Does the highest governance body consider economic issues when overseeing major capital allocation decisions?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: CDSB (REQ-02). Major decisions include expenditures, acquisitions and divestures.

questions.text: Does the highest governance body consider environmental issues when overseeing major capital allocation decisions?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: CDSB (REQ-02). Major decisions include expenditures, acquisitions and divestures.

questions.text: Does the highest governance body consider social issues when overseeing major capital allocation decisions?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: CDSB (REQ-02). Major decisions include expenditures, acquisitions and divestures.

questions.text: How does the highest governance body consider these issues in major expenditure decisions?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: CDSB (REQ-02). Describe the process or criteria used.

questions.text: How does the highest governance body consider these issues in acquisitions?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: CDSB (REQ-02). Describe the process or criteria used.

questions.text: How does the highest governance body consider these issues in divestures?
questions.hint: Risk and opportunity oversight · Source: CDSB (REQ-02). Describe the process or criteria used.
